evals.prompt: Design and build a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript prototype for an internal service-request triage screen. Use synthetic records only. Operators need to find the oldest unassigned urgent request, assign it, and recover from a failed assignment without losing their place. The current screen is a flat table with title, priority, age, owner, status, and an Assign button; all rows have equal emphasis and failures appear only in a page banner. There are 240 requests in normal use. Preserve search and filters and support desktop and narrow screens. We have no user study or production telemetry; stakeholders suspect missed urgent requests but that is unverified. Deliver your recommended direction and a concise rationale with an actionable verification plan. Do not claim user or assistive-technology testing that you did not perform. Do not access external services or real records. Use local assets when available. You may create a small representative synthetic data set rather than all 240 rows.
evals.expected_output: Runnable local prototype and evidence-qualified rationale; a controlled transfer check, not general certification.

assertions.criterion: Defines observable task-success or recovery criteria before presenting its visual recommendation; proposed targets are clearly not measured results.
Separately identifies supplied constraints, available observations, and unvalidated assumptions without inventing user findings.
Provides current experience and one plausible alternative under matching content, viewport, theme and task state, with concrete tradeoffs.
States what evidence would change a consequential recommendation.
Proposes a relevant representative-user task and uncertainty-driven follow-up, without treating a fixed participant count as proof.
Prototype supports finding an urgent unassigned request and assigning it, with observable completion feedback.
A reproducible failed assignment preserves user context and provides a usable retry or recovery route.
Search/filter no-results and assignment submitting, failure and success states are implemented with clear feedback.
Rendered desktop and narrow layouts preserve relevant information and operable controls without material clipping or overlap.
Browser verification confirms keyboard operation, accessible control names and visible focus for the implemented task.
Distinguishes rendered/source/browser evidence from representative-user and AT evidence, with unperformed checks explicitly unverified.

evals.notes: New synthetic transfer case. Same prompt, criteria, model, reasoning and host for both releases. One pair is not repeatability evidence; users and AT remain untested unless separately executed.
